dissents.topic: Whether the doc should include a working end-to-end example showing how preview() is actually invoked at runtime (e.g. via Kedro-Viz vs ad hoc)

positions.position: The current 'Get the node / Generate preview' snippet is enough to unblock users; Viz integration can be linked separately.
Without showing the intended consumer of preview() (Viz, CLI, or programmatic), users may build preview_fns that don't render anywhere useful. The doc should state where preview() is consumed.

dissents.topic: Whether 'Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs directly' is the right API design to document approvingly

positions.position: Documenting the closure workaround entrenches a limitation; the doc should at least flag that this is a known constraint tracked against the feature.
The feature is explicitly experimental; documenting the closure pattern is fine and matches today's API.

issues.description: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is an awkward and misleading way to fetch a single node
issues.detail: In the Basic usage example, `training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` but obscures intent and suggests iteration is required. Worse, it implies the first node in `pipeline.nodes` is guaranteed to be `train_model_node`, which is not true in general (Kedro topologically sorts nodes). Prefer `training_node = pipeline.nodes[0]` for a single-node pipeline, or filter by name: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes if n.name == 'train_model_node')`.

issues.description: Second `node(...)` snippets are orphaned — not wrapped in a Pipeline and reference undefined functions
issues.detail: The Mermaid customization and Text preview sections show bare `node(func=process_data, ...)` and `node(func=calculate_metrics, ...)` calls referencing `process_data` / `calculate_metrics` that are never defined in the doc. These read as runnable but will NameError if copy-pasted. Either wrap them in a `Pipeline([...])` block with stub function definitions, or mark them clearly as illustrative fragments.
issues.lines: Mermaid section (~line 490) and Text preview section (~line 590)

issues.description: `preview_from_dataframe` / `preview_from_polars` are presented as preview_fns but take arguments, contradicting the stated API contract
issues.detail: Later the doc states 'Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs directly. They're independent functions that you define.' But the Table preview section shows `def preview_from_dataframe(df: pd.DataFrame) -> TablePreview` and `def preview_from_polars(df) -> TablePreview` as if they could be passed as `preview_fn=`. They cannot — `preview_fn` is called with no arguments. This will confuse users; either rename them to helpers (e.g. `_to_table_preview(df)`) or show them being wrapped in a closure as the later section recommends.

issues.description: ImagePreview example has unreachable code after `return`
issues.detail:
```python
return ImagePreview(content="https://example.com/correlation_matrix.png")

# Or a data URI for inline images
# return ImagePreview(content="data:image/png;base64,...")
```
The second `return` is commented out, which is fine, but the structure — one function with a return followed by 'Or a ...' alternative — is confusing for readers who copy-paste. Split into two distinct example functions (`preview_from_url`, `preview_from_data_uri`) so each is a self-contained valid example.

issues.description: CustomPreview example contains literal `...` ellipses inside content dict
issues.detail: `{"type": "network_graph", "nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}` uses bare `...` as placeholder values. In Python these are valid (`Ellipsis`), but they will serialize oddly and confuse readers who expect JSON-compatible content. Replace with concrete sample entries or string placeholders like `"<list of nodes>"` with a comment.

issues.description: Inconsistent capitalization: `polars` added to ignore.txt while `Polars` already exists
issues.detail: .github/styles/Kedro/ignore.txt now lists both `Polars` and `polars`. If the Vale rule is case-insensitive this is harmless duplication; if case-sensitive, prefer documenting the canonical capitalization (Polars) and updating the doc accordingly. The doc itself uses 'polars DataFrame' (lowercase) which is why the entry was added — but the project convention seems to be 'Polars'.

issues.description: Double space in admonition link text
issues.detail: `Experimental features follow the process described in  [`docs/about/experimental.md`]` has two spaces before the link. Minor cosmetic issue but worth fixing while touching this file.

issues.description: Missing language tag on triple-backtick mermaid string and inconsistent indentation inside content strings
issues.detail: Mermaid `content` strings vary between leading-indented (multiline string with extra spaces) and flush-left. The leading indentation will be preserved in the rendered Mermaid input and may break some strict Mermaid parsers. Recommend using `textwrap.dedent(...)` or showing flush-left content consistently.

issues.description: Best practices item references external doc without verifying anchor
issues.detail: Link to `https://docs.kedro.org/projects/kedro-viz/en/stable/preview_datasets/` in best practices — verify this URL is current; Kedro-Viz docs have moved structure before. A broken link in a Best Practices section is high-visibility.

issues.description: PR checklist self-reports 'no tests added' and 'no RELEASE.md entry'
issues.detail: The PR is docs-only, so missing tests is acceptable. However, a RELEASE.md note announcing the new `preview_fn` parameter and its docs is typically expected for a user-visible feature — even an experimental one. Confirm whether the parent feature PR (#5317) already covers the release note; otherwise add one here.

issues.description: 'JSON metadata, table samples, charts, or diagrams' list in Overview duplicates the following bullet list
issues.detail: The intro paragraph enumerates payload types and then the bullet list immediately below restates them with more detail. Pick one — likely keep the bullet list and trim the intro to 'Preview payloads can take several forms (see below).' Minor prose polish.

review.summary: The PR is a docs-only addition introducing the experimental `preview_fn` parameter on TaskNode and the various `*Preview` content types. The content is comprehensive and well organized, but several code snippets are subtly wrong or inconsistent in ways that will mislead copy-paste users: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is presented as the way to fetch a specific node, two `node(...)` blocks reference undefined functions and live outside any Pipeline, and the Table preview section shows preview functions that take a DataFrame argument while a later section explicitly states preview functions take no arguments. No P0 issues — nothing here blocks merge — but the P1 fixes are quick and would materially improve the doc's reliability. Minor cosmetic issues (double space, ignore.txt casing duplication, ellipsis placeholders) round out the review.
